about: Stages and settings for the new project playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks and the outcomes each stage can record. The other keys are read by the assistant following SKILL.md. Each key is explained under notes.

playbook_for.data blockers: the fixing skill the stage named (tracking, feeds and IDs are developer fixes, not a playbook)
playbook_for.configuration fixes: the dashboard change the stage gave, then playbook-findability
playbook_for.search and category problems: playbook-findability, or playbook-test-and-learn when a merchandising rule may be the cause
playbook_for.weekly routine: playbook-weekly-triage, every Monday from the second week

stages.name: overview
stages.do: Get oriented in the Engagement project: its data, its main events and their names.

stages.name: readiness
stages.do: Run the go-live checklist for both products, using the event names the overview found.

stages.name: tracking
stages.do: Check Engagement event volumes, junk events and property fill rates.

stages.name: feeds
stages.do: Check the Discovery pixel, catalog feed and index jobs, Data Hub and Engagement catalog jobs and mapping.

stages.name: catalog-config
stages.do: Review the Discovery catalog's attribute settings against what the feed fills.

stages.name: lifecycle
stages.do: Map which of the eight lifecycle flows run, and size the gaps.

notes.plan_days: How many days the plan covers, from the day the run started: the first month of the project.
notes.plan_order: The order the plan puts its work in. Data comes first because every report and test after it depends on tracking and feeds; configuration next because it sits under every search and category page; then flows, then merchandising, then the weekly routine that keeps it going.
notes.playbook_for: Which playbook, or skill, takes each part of the plan, in words. The playbooks are separate skills, so when one isn't installed, name the skill the stage linked instead; in plan.json, next_skill is always one skill name.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, and product (the stage needs Discovery or Engagement: status suggests skipping it when the run doesn't have that product). The 30-day plan isn't a stage: no skill does it.
